newsitem.title: FINLAND: Niinisto has no comment on final markka-euro rate.
newsitem.headline: Niinisto has no comment on final markka-euro rate.

text.p: Finnish Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto said on Wednesday he did not want to discuss the final exchange rate or the timetable of the irrevocable fixing of the markka to Europe's future euro currency.
"I do not want to discuss the final exchange rate ... or the timetable, it would not be appropriate," Niinisto told a news conference.
If Finland joined the third stage of European economic and monetary union (EMU) in the first wave of countries, the markka would be linked to the euro from January, 1, 1999. @

Finance ministry permanent under-secretary of state Johnny Akerholm, one of two Finnish members of the EU monetary committee, said the decision on the final markka-euro exchange rate would not be up to Finland alone.
"The council of ministers will make the final decision," he said.
Another senior official said the EU commission would propose the exchange rates at which the national currencies joining the single currency would be fixed to the euro. @
The markka joined Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM) in October 1996. In that systen, its central parity rate to the ecu is 5.85424
